reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR03 campus in Hillsboro occupies 182,000 square feet of technical space. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for this facility, so no IT load, critical power, or rack-density translation is possible from the data available. Without a published power number, the campus cannot be ranked among the six Oregon facilities that do publish capacity figures, and it sits outside the 182 MW total those six facilities account for.

That absence of published power data is itself a signal. Oregon's 133 mapped facilities include many that publish no specifications at all, and POR03 is currently one of them. No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so no statement can be made about what redundancy tier or compliance posture the campus carries. Tenants, pricing, and grid interconnection details are not published.

For a reader evaluating AI relevance, the square footage alone is large enough to matter if the power density is there, but density is exactly what the data does not reveal. A 182,000-square-foot technical floor could support anywhere from a few dozen to several hundred high-density AI racks depending on power allocation, cooling architecture, and fit-out, none of which are published. Until Stack Infrastructure publishes a critical IT load figure for POR03, this campus cannot be assessed against Oregon peers or placed in any ranking of AI-capable capacity.
